newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:
Spokesmen Jean-Christophe Filori, Peter Guilford and Josep Coll i Carbo briefed on Monday and Tuesday's General Affairs Council in Luxembourg.

Filori said the Commission hoped that Turkey would agree, during the EU/Turkey Association Council, on the text adopted in July following its dispute with Greece. He said the approval would be a major political step and could unblock the EU-Turkey financial protocol.
Filori said discussions would also focus on Poland's and Hungary's applications to join the EU, the situation in Albania, former Yugoslavia and Belarus.
Guilford said the foreign ministers would discuss future policy on Community preferential trade agreements, textile imports and the EU/U.S. summit to take place in The Hague at the end of the month.
Coll i Carbo said Commissioner Manuel Marin and Dutch Foreign Affairs Minister Hans van Mierlo would sign cooperation agreements on behalf of the EU with Laos and Cambodia.
He also said the ministers would discuss over lunch the follow-up to the April Malta Euro-Med Conference and relations with Iran.

In answer to a question, Coll i Carbo said the Presidency would prepare a declaration on Iran condemning external support for terrorist actions and raising the possibility of banning visits by high level civil servants and ministers to the EU. He said ministers and the political committee could decide to take stronger action.

Spokesman Patrick Child said the Commission shared the general view expressed by the International Monetary Fund that it would be important, when fixing the parities for the establishment of the euro, to ensure that markets receive sufficient reassurance that the transition would involve as little exchange rate turbulence as possible.

Spokesman Filippo di Robilant said the situation in Eastern Zaire was not on the General Affairs Council agenda but that the Commission was following the situation very closely and Commissioner Emma Bonino would attend the Council.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/358: Somalia: Commission approves humanitarian aid plan worth ECU 3.7 million.
- IP/97/359: EU publishers' forum bringing information closer to the citizen.
- Speech/97/97: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn on social cohesion and employment - the role of the structural funds.
- Speech/97/98: Speech by Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies on "spotlight on cohesion policy".
- Speech/97/99: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler on sustainalble rural development in support of a sustained cohesion policy.
- Speech/97/100: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "building the Europe of the XXIst century".
- Speech/97/101: Speech by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy at the IMF Interim Committee.
- Eurostat news release No 31/97: EU's "richest" and "poorest" regions.
- Eurostat - statistics in focus - Regions No 1997-1: Per capita GDP in the regions of the European Union.
- ME97/28.4: Midday Express.
